habitat: Subtropical/tropical moist montane forests; rocky streams and gullies in mountains
story: Few birds capture the imagination quite like the Bornean Whistling Thrush (Myophonus borneensis). As a member of the Muscicapidae family, it has carved out a unique niche in Subtropical/tropical moist montane forests; rocky streams and gullies in mountains. Its conservation status is Least Concern (LC), a classification that drives crucial research and protection efforts. The Bornean Whistling Thrush's presence is a vital sign of its ecosystem's health, making its preservation a priority. This poster is a tribute to the Bornean Whistling Thrush, celebrating its role in the natural world and inspiring a deeper appreciation for biodiversity.
